question: What are the three central problems of an economy? Explain briefly.
options: 1) What to produce? Deciding which goods/services and quantities to produce given limited resources. 2) How to produce?
explanation: 1) What to produce? Deciding which goods/services and quantities to produce given limited resources. 2) How to produce? Choosing production technique (Labor-intensive vs Capital-intensive). 3) For whom to produce? Determining distribution of national income and output among citizens.

explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative foregone when a choice is made. Example: If a firm uses a piece of land to build a factory rather than renting it out for Rs. 50,000/month, the foregone Rs. 50,000 rent is the opportunity cost. Key points: Definition mentioning 'next best alternative foregone', Clear numerical or practical economic example

question: Explain why the Production Possibility Curve is concave to the origin.
options: 1) PPC is concave to the origin because of increasing Marginal Opportunity Cost (MOC). 2) Resources are specialized and
explanation: 1) PPC is concave to the origin because of increasing Marginal Opportunity Cost (MOC). 2) Resources are specialized and not equally efficient in producing all goods. 3) When shifting resources from Good Y (Butter) to Good X (Guns), progressively less efficient resources are transferred. 4) Consequently, to produce each additional unit of Good X, an increasing quantity of Good Y must be sacrificed. 5) Increasing MOC causes the slope (Delta Y / Delta X) to steepen, producing a concave curve.
